title: Bridging Option and Result
goal: Convert an Option into a Result when a missing value counts as an error.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Morning: Option and Result

sections.text: Functions in Rust use `Option` for missing values and `Result` for operations that can fail. Sometimes an `Option` needs to become a `Result` so an error can propagate.

sections.caption: ok_or converts None into an Err variant.

sections.text: `ok_or` turns `Some(v)` into `Ok(v)` and `None` into `Err(e)`. Once converted, the `?` operator can return early if the value was missing.
If creating the error value allocates memory or takes work, use `ok_or_else` with a closure instead.

sections.caption: ok_or_else evaluates the error lazily.

sections.text: Converting errors between different failure types is covered in the next section.

explanation: Convert an Option into a Result when a missing value counts as an error.
